Guide

Volterra and the Val di Cecina

San Dalmazio lies in the Val di Cecina, between Volterra and the sea, in one of the quieter corners of Tuscany. Few tour buses come this way. These are the places we love, with driving times from the house.

By Daniel & Eva, owners of Casa La Fonte

Volterra · 30 minutes

Etruscan walls and the Porta all'Arco, a Roman theatre, the Etruscan collection of the Guarnacci museum, alabaster workshops and the Piazza dei Priori, one of Italy's most beautiful squares. Stay for an aperitivo when the day visitors have left.

The geothermal valley · 15–30 minutes

Larderello, birthplace of geothermal power, with its museum; the steaming trails of the Biancane; and the warm springs of Sasso Pisano. The same energy heats Casa La Fonte. Our thermal springs guide has the details.

Villages close by · 10–15 minutes

Montecastelli Pisano for its hilltop lanes and CI.RI.SO; Pomarance for shopping and La Dispensa. In San Dalmazio itself, Stefano's family restaurant La Rocca is a minute's walk from the house, and the trail up to the Rocca Sillana starts in the village.

Day trips · about an hour

San Gimignano and Siena; Massa Marittima with its cathedral square; Bolgheri, its cypress avenue and wine estates, and the beaches of the Etruscan Coast. Pisa and Florence fit well into arrival or departure day.

Good to know

  • A car is essential. The roads wind, so allow a little more time than the map says.
  • Visit Volterra and San Gimignano early in the morning or late in the day.
  • Book the area's Michelin-starred restaurants well ahead.

Driving times are approximate, from the house in San Dalmazio.

Stay with us

Casa La Fonte is a 400-year-old stone farmhouse with a guesthouse and a private heated saltwater pool in San Dalmazio, for up to seven guests. Dogs are welcome.
